cards.title: Hormuz talks remain stalled as Iran signals a harder line
cards.summary: AP reported that the 60-day deadline passed without a visible compromise on reopening Hormuz, while Reuters reported an Iranian warning of a more offensive posture if diplomacy fails.
detail: Associated Press reported on Aug. 17 that the 60-day deadline set by the June Versailles agreement had arrived while the two sides remained further apart. Talks have focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the U.S. blockade, but AP reported no sign of a compromise or detailed nuclear negotiations. Reuters separately reported an Iranian official’s warning that Tehran could shift from a defensive to a fully offensive posture if diplomacy fails.

The unresolved waterway question matters beyond diplomacy: Hormuz carried about a fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas before the war, so navigation, insurance, and energy-price risk remain linked to the talks. The UAE’s earlier attribution of tanker attacks to Iran is still an attributed claim, not a completed independent finding.

The next evidence is concrete movement on access through the strait, the blockade, and a verifiable negotiating channel. Until those appear, the deadline is a marker of stalled diplomacy rather than proof of a settled end-state.
cards.why: The deadline has passed, but the waterway and negotiating channel remain unresolved as new escalation language enters the public record.

cards.title: U.S. stocks rebound as Treasury buybacks ease bond pressure
cards.summary: AP reported a first gain in four sessions on Wednesday: S&P 500 +0.2%, Dow +0.2% and Nasdaq +0.2%, after Treasury announced larger long-duration buybacks.
detail: Associated Press reported that the S&P 500 rose 0.2% to 7,707.98, the Dow gained 0.2% to 53,463.05 and the Nasdaq added 0.2% to 26,331.09 on Wednesday, Aug. 19. It was the S&P’s first gain in four sessions.

AP linked the rebound to the Treasury Department’s plan to at least double planned purchases of longer-term Treasurys from Sept. 9 through Nov. 4, which pushed 10- and 30-year yields lower during the session. Company earnings also supported the move, while AI-linked stocks remained uneven.
This is a completed-session description, not a forecast. The next uncertainty is whether the yield relief lasts and how investors interpret the Fed minutes’ inflation language.

cards.summary: Minutes from the July meeting say many officials would likely support higher rates if inflation fails to decline, even as the September decision remains uncertain.
detail: The Federal Reserve released minutes from its July 28–29 meeting on Aug. 19. AP reported that many officials thought the central bank might need to lift its short-term rate in coming months if inflation did not subside; the committee had voted 9–3 to keep the rate near 3.6%.

The minutes identified inflation risks from the Iran war, tariffs and heavy AI-infrastructure investment. AP also reported that investors still expected the Fed to hold in September, while noting that market expectations could change.
The next evidence is incoming inflation, energy and labor data rather than a predetermined policy move. This card describes the policy signal and carries no investment recommendation.
